correctness.rationale: For the leading map, the fold equation is F_lambda=h_lambda-K h_lambda'=0. The C2 expansion gives F_lambda/lambda=(g-Kg')+O_C1(lambda); the simple-root condition gives x_f=x_*+O(lambda). Since g(x_*)>0, log h_lambda(x_f)=log lambda+log g(x_*)+O(lambda), hence theta_f=K log(1/lambda)+C+O(lambda). Its derivative is -K/lambda+O(1), which yields unique phase locks and the stated limiting ratio. The proof is analytic and the claim explicitly limits itself to phase-locked fold returns.
